summary: Grenada's visa list, published by its Embassy in Washington, marks nationals of countries including the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom 'No Visa required'. 'Port of Entry' means a visa granted on arrival in Grenada, for which the Embassy arranges a pre-clearance letter from the Immigration and Passport Office beforehand; 'Prior to Arrival' means the visa must be obtained at one of Grenada's missions or consulates before travel. CARICOM Heads of Government recorded in 2008 that Grenada had acted to grant CARICOM nationals a definite entry of six months.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Grenada?
faq.answer: Grenada's visa list, published by its Embassy in Washington, marks nationals of countries including the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia and New Zealand 'No Visa required'. Nationals marked 'Port of Entry' are granted a visa on arrival in Grenada; the Embassy arranges a pre-clearance letter from the Immigration and Passport Office for them before travel. Nationals marked 'Prior to Arrival' must obtain a visa at one of Grenada's missions or consulates before travel. CARICOM Heads of Government recorded in 2008 that Grenada had acted to grant CARICOM nationals a definite entry of six months.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Grenada without a visa?
faq.answer: Grenada's visa list states a period for some nationalities (30 days for Argentina and China, 60 for Cuba, 90 for Brazil) and says visitors granted entry for a set period are required to obtain a visa when remaining beyond it. The UK government says British visitors are allowed to stay for a maximum of 3 months on entry; Canada's travel advice says no tourist visa is required for stays up to 90 days and that to stay longer you must obtain proper authorization at the Immigration and Passport Department in St. George's. CARICOM Heads of Government recorded in 2008 that Grenada had acted to grant CARICOM nationals a definite entry of six months.

faq.question: Is there an arrival form for Grenada?
faq.answer: No official source we could read describes Grenada's arrival form or says whether it can be completed online. The UK government says you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Grenada?
faq.answer: WHO's country list says Grenada requires proof of yellow fever vaccination for travellers aged 1 year or over arriving from countries with risk of yellow fever transmission, and for travellers who have transited for more than 12 hours through an airport of such a country. WHO's list of countries with risk of yellow fever transmission includes Trinidad and Tobago, where the risk is present only in parts of the country.

faq.question: Can I drive in Grenada on my own license?
faq.answer: Canada's travel advice says that to drive in Grenada you must have a local driver's licence, which you can purchase from a car rental agency or the central police station in St. George's by showing your valid driver's licence, and that traffic drives on the left.

faq.question: Does CARICOM free movement apply in Grenada?
faq.answer: Yes. CARICOM Heads of Government recorded in March 2008 that Grenada had acted to implement the decision that CARICOM nationals travelling to other Member States be granted a definite entry of six months, subject to the right of Member States to reject undesirable persons and to prevent persons from becoming a charge on public funds.

tips.hurricane-season.text: The hurricane season is from early June to the end of November in the Atlantic, Caribbean Sea and Gulf of Mexico.
Hurricane Beryl made landfall on the islands of Carriacou and Petite Martinique in July 2024, and there continues to be reduced tourist infrastructure as rebuilding efforts continue.

entryRequirements.travelInsurance.text: The main government hospital can cope with many types of treatment but serious cases may need emergency evacuation. Medical treatment in Grenada can be expensive. Make sure you have adequate travel health insurance

entryRequirements.onwardTicket.text: If you are visiting our islands, you must have a valid passport and return or onward ticket.
Customs officials will ask you to show them a return or onward ticket to enter Grenada. They may also ask for a proof of sufficient funds to cover your stay.

countryFacts.safety.text: Most crime in Grenada is non-violent and opportunistic, such as thefts of unattended items or burglaries from villas or cars. There are occasional violent crimes including armed robbery and sexual assault.
Currents can be deceptively strong and not all beaches have lifeguards or warning flags.
The hurricane season in the Caribbean normally runs from June to November.

visaTypes.visitor-visa.feeNotes.text: Application for a Single –Entry Visa is US$200.00 per applicant. Application for a Multiple–Entry Visa is US$375.00 per applicant.
Applications MUST be made at least 6 weeks PRIOR to departure date.
The processing time for the application is approximately ten (10) business days from date of receipt.

visaTypes.port-of-entry-visa.feeNotes.text: If the Pre-Clearance letter is issued by the Immigration and Passport Office of Grenada, upon arrival in Grenada the fee for a Single–Entry Visa is EC$200.00 per applicant and the fee for a Multiple–Entry Visa is EC$375.00 per applicant.
The Fee for a Pre-Clearance letter from the Immigration and Passport Office of Grenada is US$10.00 payable to Embassy of Grenada.
The processing time for the application is approximately ten (10) business days from date of receipt of application at the Embassy.

countryFacts.driving.text: Before visitors get behind the wheel, they must first secure a Grenadian driving permit, which can be obtained by providing a valid driver’s license at the police station.
A fee of EC$60 is required. Some rental companies provide drivers with a local permit as part of their service.

entryRequirements.overstay.text: 14. Visitors and passengers in transit (1) Where a person desires to remain in Grenada as a visitor or passenger in transit for a period not exceeding twelve months, an immigration officer may, if so requested, without deciding whether that person is or is not a prohibited alien, grant him or her a permit to remain in Grenada for such period not exceeding twelve m onths as may be specified in the permit.

(4) If a visitor or passenger in transit remains in Grenada after the expiration of his or her permit without having presented himself or herself as aforesaid he or she shall be deemed to be a prohibited alien and may be dealt with as such.

18. Removal orders by magistrate If a person is held to be a prohibited alien, then, subject to the provisions of this Act and the terms of any permit granted to him or her thereunder, a magistrate may, on the application of an immigration officer or a person deputed in writing by the Chief Immigration Officer for the purpose of making such application make an order requiring the alien to be removed from Grenada and in the meantime to be detained in custody.
